comparison: Perfect agreement on axonal enrichment of Wnd (C2, C35-C37, C40-C41). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. However, Reviewer 3 raises concern about requiring hiw mutants or wnd overexpression to see enrichment, questioning physiological relevance - a concern not reflected in OpenEval's evaluation.

Perfect agreement on compartment-specific turnover (C3, C47-C48). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewer 2 notes uncertainty about whether this is due to restricted Hiw localization, which OpenEval does not address in this result but discusses in R34.

Both address deletion mapping (C49-C52) and palmitoylation (C53-C60). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this extends prior work on DLK palmitoylation to in vivo context, indicating it's not entirely novel - a contextual point OpenEval addresses separately in R22.

OpenEval R4 focuses on palmitoylation evidence (C53-C57, C59-C60), which overlaps with peer R3's evaluation of palmitoylation findings. Both SUPPORTED, though peer review emphasizes this extends prior cell culture work to in vivo.

Both address Golgi localization of Wnd-C130S and dHIP14 involvement (C62-C63, C65-C71). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on these mechanistic details but accept them as supporting data.

Both address dysregulated protein turnover with C130S mutation (C73-C76). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 also includes claims C5-C6 about the general principle of transport-dependent degradation.
Both address retained signaling capacity of Wnd-C130S (C81-C86). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 also includes downstream consequences (C87-C93) that OpenEval addresses in separate results R8-R9.
OpenEval R8 addresses enhanced signaling at lower expression (C87-C88), which peer R5 includes as part of broader evaluation of hyperactivation consequences. Both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R9 addresses eye phenotypes (C89-C91), which peer R5 includes in broader evaluation of hyperactivation consequences. Both SUPPORTED, though OpenEval suggests photoreceptor quantification would strengthen interpretation.
Both address Rab screening identifying Rab11 (C97-C98). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer review views the screening approach as a strength and notes it identifies a novel genetic interaction.

Both address Rab11 colocalization (C102-C106). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, but peer review evaluates as UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'how Rab11 is involved...is not resolved as it is clear that Rab11 is not travelling with Wnd to the axon' - a key disagreement on mechanistic understanding.

Both address Rab11's role in Wnd turnover (C107-C113). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the mRNA reduction interpretation as speculative; peer reviewers accept the post-translational mechanism as convincing.
Both address pharmacological rescue with DLKi (C119-C121). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer R9 also includes genetic rescue data (C122-C125) that OpenEval addresses in R14.
Both address rescue of Rab11 phenotypes (C122-C125). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer review views convergence of pharmacological and genetic rescue as convincing evidence for causal relationship.

Both address overall model and conclusions (C14-C15, C126-C132). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer review calls it 'important new insights' but notes mechanistic details about Rab11 remain unclear - consistent with peer R7's UNCERTAIN evaluation.

OpenEval R38 addresses mechanistic conclusions about protein-based transport (C134-C135), which peer R11 includes in overall model evaluation. Both SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes direct visualization would strengthen conclusions.

OpenEval R39 addresses conclusions about Rab11's role (C114-C115), which peer R8 evaluates as part of turnover evidence. Both SUPPORTED, with peer review emphasizing convergence of multiple approaches.
OpenEval R40 addresses conclusions about failed turnover consequences (C92-C93), which peer R5 includes in broader hyperactivation evaluation. Both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R42 addresses mechanistic conclusions about Rab11's sorting role (C146-C148). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with caveats, while peer R7 evaluates related claims as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanism is 'not resolved.'

Both address speculation about disease relevance (C153, C166). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct disease model testing; peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED but acknowledges it remains speculative.
